topic.description: a subject in the knowledge graph. Any entity may be one by wearing this: a subject of its own is topic + doc + content, and a project is its own topic, so what is known about it sits under it. What a topic belongs to is whatever contains it: one about a project sits under the project, and one about the world under none. Its doc is the cover: the title, and a line or two saying what belongs under it. Its content.body is the contents: what is understood about it, written as one document citing its sources. Its edges say what it holds (contains: a subtopic, or anything else, such as a memory, a design, a skill, a package or somebody's words), what to understand first (requires), what it reads or references, and what it cites; beliefs are about it (belief.about). A session opened on it (session.topic) starts from its tree, compiled (topic_read)

name.description: the title in lowercase, its spaces single; no two topics share one, so a name said again finds the topic that has it. A name, not an identity: it changes with the title, and the entity keeps its eid

topic.description: the topic it was opened on: the topic tree compiled from it (topic_read) opens its context, after its persona's

topic_read.title: Read a topic as a session's context
topic_read.description: Read a topic as the context a session opened on it is given (session_new with topic): one markdown document with the topics that contain it, its cover, its contents and their $was token, everything it holds in full (a long body cut, with the id to read the rest), the topics below it as an outline, and what to understand first, what is related and its sources, one line each. Returns text in content.body.

topic_new.title: Make a topic
topic_new.description: Make a topic, where no existing topic fits; a project is already its own topic. name is what it is called, as plain and general as the subject is ("testing", "ui components", "naming"), never a phrase about one point; body is its cover, a line or two saying what belongs under it, never a point anybody made. It belongs to whatever contains it, so its name and cover never say the project: put one about a project under the project with topic_add. One name is one topic: a name that is taken is refused with the topic that has it, to use instead, and so is a name whose words hold another topic's or are held by them ("economic market design" beside "market design"). Returns the applied bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components); the topic's id is its entity.eid.

name.description: what the topic is called, a few plain words

body.description: a line or two saying what belongs under it

topic_find.title: Find topics
topic_find.description: Find existing topics: those whose name, title or cover holds each word in said, as the start of a word or by its stem ("data modeling" finds "data model", "tests" finds "testing"), ranked by meaning to the entity near names when the server has a vector index, or, given neither, the topics in order of name. Use it to find what is known about a subject (graph_show on a topic lists what it holds), before putting something you wrote under its topic (topic_add), and before making a topic, with near set to what you are filing under one, so a subject already named is reused rather than named again in other words. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components), each whole; limit defaults to 12.

said.description: words the topic's name, title or cover holds, as the start of a word or by its stem

near.description: an entity id or name whose meaning ranks the topics

topic_add.title: Add to a topic
topic_add.description: Put entities under a topic, where whoever reads the topic finds them: a memory, a design, a skill, a package, somebody's words, or a subtopic. Each gets a contains edge from the topic; adding one already there changes nothing, and drop takes them out instead. One entity may sit under several topics. Find the topic first with topic_find, or make one with topic_new; a project is its own topic, so its id or name places things under it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

topic.description: the topic's id or title, or a project's

ids.description: the entities to put under it, by id

drop.description: take them out of the topic instead
